Summary.value: New Street Research “$4tn AI capex in 2030” (18-Sep-2026) vs Capstone — summary

NSR (Pierre Ferragu, Antoine Chkaiban, Benjamin Harwood, Peter Vogel) raised its 2030 AI capex forecast from ~$3.1tn to $4.15tn. This workbook transcribes the note with live formulas (NSR_* sheets), lays the Capstone series beside it (House) and compares them line by line (Comparison). This page links to those cells.

• $4.15tn of AI infrastructure capex in 2030 (from $584bn in 2025, 48% CAGR): XPUs $1.70tn (41%), other equipment & buildings $1.02tn (24%), networking $465bn, DRAM & NAND $423bn, other server content $373bn, CPUs $168bn. Increase is volume-driven; ~275 GW of installed AI capacity in 2030 (from ~225 GW).
• Memory share of AI infrastructure keeps rising even as prices normalise: HBM $560bn in 2030 (33% of XPU spend, GM ~76%), DRAM $241bn, NAND $182bn.

• Hyperscalers: group capex $8.7tn cumulative 2026-30, FCF negative through 2029 (trough −$486bn in 2028), positive again in 2030; OCF $8.0tn vs consensus $6tn on a 24% revenue CAGR and 77% incremental OCF margin.

• Funding: $16.5tn of datacenter capex 2026-30, >75% covered by hyperscaler / tier-2 / neocloud OCF and enterprise self-funding; ~$3.7tn (23%) needs external financing, mostly neoclouds with hyperscaler guarantees; industry leverage ~2.2x 2027 EBITDA.

1. Level: NSR is above the house on total AI capex in every year — $584bn vs $396bn in 2025 (+47%), $1,132 vs $902 (2026), $2,190 vs $1,885 (2027), $3,330 vs $2,913 (2028, +14%). The gap narrows because the house grows faster in 2026-27 (+128% / +109% vs NSR +94% / +93%).

2. 2030: NSR $4.15tn vs the house's July-vintage extension $3.48tn (−16%). Re-based on the current CY28 ($2,913bn) the same growth path gives ~$3.9tn — within ~6% of NSR. The house has no modeled CY29-30 on the current base.

3. Mix: the house puts more into accelerators (48% → 40% of capex) than NSR (35% → 41%); NSR puts more into shell/buildings early (44% in 2025 vs 36%) and less later (27% vs 36% in 2028). Capex per GW converges on ~$42bn by 2028 (NSR $40-45bn; house $30.5 → $41.9bn).

4. Memory is the biggest dollar disagreement: HBM 2030 NSR $560bn vs house repriced $283bn (BofA $168bn) — the two agree in 2027 (~$190bn) and diverge after, as NSR keeps HBM compounding at 22-38% into 2029-30 where the house fades price. Ex-HBM DRAM+NAND agree within 6% (2027) and 4% (2030).

5. GW: NSR ~275 GW installed in 2030 (basis unstated) sits between the house's cumulative chip-content GW (299, gross) and cumulative facility GW (242). On an online-capacity basis the house has 119 GW at CY28.

6. Hyperscaler cash: NSR OCF runs 11-19% above the house big-4; NSR capex 19-35% above in 2027-28; NSR FCF troughs at −$486bn in 2028 vs house −$261bn (house trough is earlier and shallower). Both are far below BBG consensus (−$19bn 2027 / +$132bn 2028, 07-28 vintage).

7. Cloud revenue is where the two agree most: AI cloud 2030 $1,511bn (NSR) vs $1,492bn (house), within 13% every year. Non-AI cloud diverges: NSR $370bn vs house $630bn in 2030 (NSR ~10% growth, house ~21%).

8. Funding: NSR needs $3.7tn of external financing over 2026-30 (23% of $16.5tn), mostly neoclouds. The house already shows ~$2.9tn of spend not covered by big-4 cash in 2026-28 alone (big-4 FCF −$563bn + other players' capex $2.3tn) — a bigger, earlier hole than NSR's.

9. Internal NSR inconsistencies flagged in the NSR sheets: p.5 'other server content' 2025 ($29bn) does not tie to its printed +191% growth; DRAM and NAND carry an identical COGS-growth row; p.6 financing $3.7tn vs p.8 $4.0tn; hyperscaler AI capex at $40-45bn/GW implies ~184 GW cumulative vs the stated '>100 GW'.

Comparison.value: NSR (18-Sep-2026) vs Capstone — side by side, 2025-2030

Each metric has three rows: NSR (linked from the NSR sheets) / Capstone (linked from House) / Δ = Capstone ÷ NSR − 1 (blue = Capstone above NSR, red = below). Capstone CY29-30 come from July-vintage extensions (stale base) or are blank. Read the basis note before quoting a delta.
1. THE HEADLINE — total AI capex, all buyers

NSR p.4 total (all buyers). Capstone CY25-28 = AI Model Capex Total (31-Aug, all players); CY29-30 = Semis MAP v11 scenario extension on the JULY base (CY28 2,588 vs current 2,913) — re-based on the current CY28 the CY29-30 house path would be ~$3.4tn / ~$3.9tn. Read: NSR is ABOVE the house in every year — +47% in 2025 ($584bn vs $396bn), narrowing to +14% in 2028 ($3,330bn vs $2,913bn) because the house grows faster in 2026-27. In 2030 NSR $4.15tn vs the stale house extension $3.48tn (−16%); on the re-based ~$3.9tn the gap is ~6%.
House 2026 +128% / 2027 +109% / 2028 +54% vs NSR +94% / +93% / +52% / +14% / +9%. Same 2028 deceleration; house 2027 is the steeper year.
Cumulative AI capex ($bn) — NSR 2026-30 in the 2030 column; Capstone 2026-28 in the 2028 column
NSR 2026-30 cumulative $14.6tn AI (inside a $16.5tn total DC figure). House 2026-28 alone = $5.7tn on the current model (NSR 2026-28 = $6.65tn). No house cumulative to 2030 on the current base.
2. WHO SPENDS — hyperscalers vs the rest

NSR p.7 group capex, basket not enumerated. Capstone = MSFT+AMZN+GOOG+META official models (calendar). NSR 2027 $1,384bn vs house big-4 $1,098bn: NSR is ~26% above on a basket that probably includes ORCL and possibly others.

NSR implied = group capex − non-AI ($125bn +13% p.a., NSR's own comment). Capstone = AI Model hyperscaler AI bottom-up (big-4). House is above NSR in 2025-26 (+16% / +4%) and below from 2027 (−8%) and 2028 (−21%); by 2028 both put ~all of the growth in AI.

NSR: cumulative 2026-30, neocloud $6.5tn + enterprise/gov $1.4tn = 48% of $16.5tn (neocloud alone 39%). Capstone: other players (ORCL, CRWV, SpaceX, labs, sovereign) = 24% of 2026 → 40% of 2027 → 51% of 2028 AI capex. Both houses agree the non-hyperscaler half is where the funding question lives.

NSR XPUs (incl. HBM) vs Capstone chips = designers' revenue incl. HBM (AI Model CY25-28; Semis MAP extension CY29-30). Capstone is only 2-8% below NSR on XPUs while it is 12-32% below on total capex — i.e. the house puts a LARGER share of each capex dollar into the accelerator than NSR does.
XPUs as % of total AI capex

NSR 35% → 38% (2028) → 41% (2030), rising. Capstone 48% → 40% (CY28), falling as the networking/CPU/memory bucket grows 16% → 25%. House share is higher every year but the trajectories cross — the sharpest structural disagreement in this comparison.
NSR: ~60% in 2030 (~$1.0tn NVDA of $1.7tn). Capstone: 68% CY28 (AI Model), 64% CY30 (Semis MAP). House is 4-8pp more NVDA-heavy at the end of the decade; BofA has 68% CY30.

NSR p.4 CPUs (AI) 6 → 168. Capstone Semis MAP AI CPUs (head-node, BofA-mix on house capex) 15 → 171. Nearly identical 2030 level, but the house is 1.5-2.5x NSR in 2025-26 (NSR's $6bn 2025 looks too low against any head-node count).

NSR p.5 CPUs spending 25 → 202. Capstone ledger: house build ~$55bn CY26 / $96bn CY27 / $137bn CY28, ~$180-200bn 2030 (CPU-silicon total incl. Vera + enterprise). House is above NSR in 2026-28 (front-loaded agentic 1:1), converges by 2030; AMD's $220bn 2030 is above both.

NSR networking 40 → 465. Capstone Semis MAP AI networking (BofA ratio × house accelerators) 57 → 606; Bottom_Up physical build is lower (56 → 306). NSR sits between the two house constructions; all three agree networking outgrows compute.
Networking — vs Capstone Bottom_Up physical build ($bn)
Same NSR line vs the physical units×ASP build (Bottom_Up_Capex_v3). Shows the house's own range on networking: 0.65x (2028-30) to 1.4x (2025) of NSR.
Other equipment & buildings / shell, power, site ($bn)

NSR 258 → 1,016 (44% → 24% of capex, 'frontloaded'). Capstone AI Model 'Other' 141 → 1,041 CY25-28 (held ~36% of capex). NSR has ~$120bn MORE shell in 2025 and ~$140bn LESS by 2028 — NSR front-loads the physical build, the house scales it with chips.
Shell / other equipment as % of total AI capex
See above. NSR's falling share is the mechanism behind its 'financing is easy' conclusion (less long-lived asset per capex dollar over time).
HBM ($bn) — vs Capstone AI Model bottom-up

NSR HBM 34 → 560 (33% of XPU by 2030, GM normalizing to 76%). Capstone AI Model HBM Model (units × GB × spec-sheet $/GB) 27 → 282 CY25-28. House CY28 is 15% below NSR; the house has NO 2027 repricing in this line.
HBM ($bn) — vs Capstone Semis MAP repriced (bits × $/GB)

Same NSR line vs Semis MAP repriced HBM (2/4.3/6.25/8/9.6/11.2 EB × $17.5/18/31/28/26.6/25.3 per GB). House 2027 ($194bn) matches NSR ($189bn); by 2030 NSR is 2.0x the house ($560bn vs $283bn) — NSR keeps HBM $ compounding at +22-38% into 2029-30 where the house fades price. BofA CY30 is $168bn.
NSR 16% → 33%. Capstone AI Model 14% → 24% (CY28). The HBM-content-per-dollar story is the same direction; NSR is more extreme.

NSR DRAM & NAND 26 → 338 (2027 peak) → 423. Capstone Semis MAP fleet DDR5 + DC NAND 42 → 317 (2027) → 405. Close in 2027 (−6%) and 2030 (−4%); the house is ~25% lower in 2028 (house DDR5 price fades from 2028 while NSR peaks there) and ~$16bn higher in 2025 (fleet DRAM already counted). Both fade price after 2027-28.
DRAM + NAND ($bn) — vs Capstone Bottom_Up 'memory bought direct'

Same NSR line vs the physical Bottom_Up build (DDR5 + DC NAND + …; broader perimeter incl. LPDDR/HDD legs). Bottom_Up runs 1.4-2.9x NSR — the sheet's own note flags stacked bull assumptions; treat as the house's upper bound.

NSR 60 → 983. Capstone Semis MAP TOTAL CSP memory bill (mapped + repricing + fleet DDR5/NAND/HDD) 90 → 737. House above NSR in 2025-26, below from 2027 as NSR keeps HBM compounding. Memory-as-%-of-capex: NSR 10% → 24% (2030); house 21% → 21%.
Total memory as % of total AI capex

House share uses the Semis MAP capex path as denominator (same vintage as its numerator). JPM Kwon (08-09) has memory at 31%/49%/60% of CSP HARDWARE capex 2026-28 — a different denominator (ex-shell); not comparable to either row.
5. GIGAWATTS — three bases, none of them NSR's
Installed AI capacity (GW) — vs Capstone cumulative CHIP-content GW

NSR ~275 GW 2030 (basis not stated; prior ~225). Capstone purchase-basis chip stock 24/51/102/171 GW CY25-28 (AI Model, all players) and Semis MAP cumulative chip-content GW 217/299 CY29-30 (gross, no retirements, July base). On this basis the house is AT NSR's 2030 mark (+9%). Chip GW ≠ facility GW.
Installed AI capacity (GW) — vs Capstone cumulative FACILITY GW

Bottom_Up_Capex_v3 physical facility GW (units × kW × PUE): 24/44/80/125/179/242 GW CY25-30. 12% below NSR's 275 in 2030; matches BofA's 233 GW. The Tokenomics bridge's BofA-derived 224 GW IT (~314 GW facility) brackets NSR from the other side.
Installed AI capacity (GW) — vs Capstone ONLINE-capacity stock

AI Model online-capacity stock 14/31/64/119 GW CY25-28 — what is actually energised and billable, ~1 year behind purchases. NSR's hyperscaler-only '>100 GW deployed by end of decade' sits closest to this basis.

NSR '~$40-45bn/GW' (midpoint 42.5, hyperscaler AI capex). Capstone blended build cost per GW added 30.5/34/38/41.9 CY25-28 (NVDA-only basis runs 37 → 51; CY28E NVDA 50.8 = chip 25.5 + networking 10.3 + other 15.0). MS GB300 all-in $39bn/GW. Converging on ~$42bn by 2028.

NSR ~$13bn/GW (AI cloud revenue / deployed GW) — but its tier-2/neocloud block implies ~$25bn/GW ($2.3tn on 91 GW). Capstone implied blend (implied AI revenue / avg online GW) ~13-14 $bn/GW; by designer NVDA $20bn, Google $14bn, Trainium $7bn. Ledger rental marks $12-13bn merchant GPU. NSR's hyperscaler figure = the house blend; its neocloud figure = the house NVDA-premium figure.
6. HYPERSCALER CASH — OCF, capex, FCF (NSR basket vs Capstone big-4, calendar)

NSR OCF 580 → 2,650 (its basket). Capstone big-4 OCF 515/688/923/1,202 CY25-28 (GOOG/META on the conservative LL+D&A definition). House is 11-19% below NSR each year — consistent with NSR's stated +$2tn OCF uplift vs consensus (24% revenue CAGR, 77% incremental OCF margin).
NSR group capex 415 → 2,387. Capstone big-4 total capex 410/750/1,163/1,463. Level agrees in 2025; NSR is 19% above the house in 2027 and 35% above in 2028 (basket + NSR's higher AI intensity).

NSR 164 / (22) / (310) / (486) / (162) / +263 — trough 2028, positive 2030, ~$700bn cumulative burn. Capstone big-4 105 / (62) / (240) / (261) CY25-28 — the house goes negative a year EARLIER and less deep (no 2029-30). BBG consensus basket (07-28): (3.5) / (18.8) / +132 — both NSR and the house are far below consensus on 2027-28 FCF.
NSR 0.72x → 1.33x (2028 peak) → 0.90x. Capstone 0.80x → 1.26x (2027) → 1.22x. Same peak intensity, house peaks a year earlier.
7. CLOUD REVENUE — the line where the two houses agree most

NSR AI cloud 55 → 1,511 ('>100 GW, ~$13bn/GW'). Capstone AI Model Resumo | Clouds (scenario 1, demand view) 50 → 1,492 CY25-30. Within 13% every year and within 1% in 2030 — built independently (house = GW × rev/GW by lab/use). The strongest convergence in the note.
NSR cloud 279 → 1,881. Capstone 283 → 2,122. House perimeter = MSFT Azure (API gross) + AWS + GCP + Others (ORCL/CRWV/neoclouds) — the 'Others' leg is why the house total is above NSR from 2028.
NSR non-AI 224 → 370 (~10% growth). Capstone 233 → 630 (+21-23% p.a.). House keeps traditional cloud compounding; NSR flattens it. This is a $260bn gap by 2030 hiding under an identical AI line.
External financing required ($tn) — NSR cumulative 2026-30 in the 2030 column; Capstone big-4 FCF shortfall 2026-28 in the 2028 column

NSR $3.7tn (23% of $16.5tn): hyperscalers ~$0.7tn (= their cumulative FCF 2026-30 of −$716bn), tier-2/neoclouds ~$3.3tn (loans 2.6 + prepay/equity 0.7) at ~2.2x 2027 EBITDA of the key players. Capstone: big-4 cumulative FCF 2026-28 = −$563bn (shown as +0.56 $tn of need), plus 'capex faltante' for other players of $152bn / $722bn / $1,450bn CY26-28 = $2.3tn that big-4 cash does not cover. The house's 2026-28 external need (~$2.9tn) is ALREADY close to NSR's five-year $3.7tn — the house sees a bigger, earlier hole.

Reading guide: a positive (blue) delta means Capstone is above NSR; red means below. Blank = no house value on a comparable basis. Every Capstone CY29-30 value is a July-2026 extension on the July AI Model base and is flagged in House column L.

README.value: NSR — “Here we are – $4tn AI capex in 2030?” — transcription + Capstone comparison
Built 2026-09-18 for Felipe Monteiro (Capstone). Workbook generated by script; every number carries its source in the row.
SOURCE NOTE

New Street Research LLP — Industry Report, 18 September 2026 — “Here we are – $4tn AI capex in 2030?”. Analysts: Pierre Ferragu, Antoine Chkaiban, Benjamin Harwood, Peter Vogel (Global Technology Research). 10 pages, 6 exhibits.
PDF: C:\Users\Felipe.monteiro\Downloads\20260918-INDUSTRY-model-update-note-1_260918_112522.pdf (copy filed in _inbox as 20260918-NSR-Ferragu-AI-capex-4tn-2030-industry-report.pdf).
PDF footer watermark: “rendered exclusively for acastro@absoluteinvest.com.br” — a client-rendered copy forwarded to Capstone; treat redistribution accordingly.

Every NSR figure is transcribed as printed (blue). Totals, growth, shares, margins and cumulatives are recomputed by formula (black) and checked against the printed values (yellow check cells should read ~0).
SHEETS
Summary — the front page: what NSR says, nine key reads, and a compact headline table (2028 / 2030) linked to the Comparison sheet.
Comparison — NSR vs Capstone side by side, 2025-2030, in rows of three (NSR / Capstone / Δ = Capstone ÷ NSR − 1) with a basis note per metric. Read the basis note before quoting any delta.
NSR_Capex — p.4 “Annual AI infrastructure capex by component, 2025-2030” ($bn) with recomputed total, YoY, mix and CAGR + reconciliation to the printed total.
NSR_Memory — p.5 “Memory economics within AI infrastructure deployments” ($bn): HBM / DRAM / NAND / CPU / other, with the additive-structure checks.
NSR_HyperPL — p.7 hyperscaler P&L and cash flow 2025-2030 (core vs cloud, EBITDA, D&A, OCF, capex, FCF) with recomputed EBIT / FCF / margins and cumulatives.
NSR_Funding — p.6 funding waterfall ($16.5tn cumulative DC capex 2026-30) + p.8 tier-2/neocloud financing structure and Debt/EBITDA.
NSR_Datapoints — p.2 supply-chain datapoints table + p.3 forecast bridge ($2.4tn → ~$3.1tn → $4.1tn) and the 2030 GW / NVDA-share / CPU marks used by the formulas.
House — Capstone series: AI Model (31-Aug-2026 save), Semis MAP v11 (16-Jul-2026), Bottom_Up_Capex_v3 (24-Jul-2026), Tokenomics bridge, funding dashboard, assumptions ledger canon.
COLOUR LEGEND

Blue = hardcoded input (NSR as printed, or a Capstone value pasted from the named file). Black = formula. Green = link to another sheet in this workbook. In the Comparison sheet, deltas print blue when Capstone is above NSR and red when below.
Yellow fill = reconciliation / check cells (should read ~0). Salmon fill = an internal inconsistency in the NSR note itself, flagged rather than fixed.
BASIS WARNINGS (wiki rules — never mix)

1. AI capex perimeter: NSR “AI capex” = all buyers (hyperscalers + tier-2/neoclouds + enterprise/government). Capstone AI Model “Capex Total” = all players (hyperscalers + ORCL/CRWV/SpaceX/labs/others). Same spirit, different enumeration.

2. Hyperscaler basket: NSR p.7 “Hyperscalers” is not enumerated in the note. Capstone big-4 = MSFT/AMZN/GOOG/META (AI Model); the 5-name FY table adds ORCL. Capstone big-4 OCF/capex/FCF are CALENDAR-year model figures; the FY table is fiscal-year.

3. GW: NSR “~275GW of installed AI capacity in 2030” does not state facility vs IT-load. Capstone carries THREE GW stocks (purchase-basis chip GW, online-capacity GW, facility GW) — each is labelled in House and Comparison. Do not net them.

4. Memory: NSR splits HBM (inside XPU) from DRAM & NAND (server). Capstone has three HBM lines (AI Model bottom-up units×GB×$/GB; Semis MAP calibrated to $35bn CY25; Semis MAP repriced bits×$/GB) and two ex-HBM memory builds. All are shown; none is netted against another.

5. CPU: NSR p.4 “CPUs” (6→168) is the AI slice; p.5 “CPUs spending” (25→202) is the total server-CPU market. Capstone Semis MAP “AI CPUs” = head-node CPUs inside AI servers; Bottom_Up “CPUs + servidores” is broader (general-purpose servers ex-memory).

6. Vintage: Capstone CY29-30 values exist only in the July-2026 Semis MAP / Bottom_Up workbooks, built on the July AI Model (CY28 capex $2,588bn). The current AI Model (31-Aug) has CY28 at $2,913bn (+13%) and stops at CY28. CY29-30 house rows are therefore STALE-BASE extensions, flagged in the House vintage column.

7. Revenue per GW: NSR ~$13bn/GW is AI-cloud revenue per deployed GW. Capstone Economics-GW revenue/GW is by designer/client (NVDA $20bn, Google $14bn, Trainium $7bn, others $10.5bn). The ledger rental marks ($12-13bn merchant GPU) are a third basis.
